title: "CI Pipelines for Distro Building"

# CI Pipelines for Distro Building

Building an operating system is not a one-time event; it is an ongoing software factory. Whenever a patch is submitted or an upstream security release is published, continuous integration pipelines must rebuild, verify, and publish updated artifacts.

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|              Automated Distro CI/CD Architecture          |
|                                                           |
| 1. Git Commit to Recipe Repo (e.g., bump curl to 8.5.1)   |
|         |                                                 |
|         v                                                 |
| 2. Change Detection & Dependency Sorting                  |
|    - Detect modified recipes in commit                    |
|    - Compute topological sort (build libcurl before curl) |
|         |                                                 |
|         v                                                 |
| 3. Distributed Build Matrix                               |
|    - Parallel build jobs: x86_64, aarch64, riscv64        |
|    - Verify build against QA linting & checksec           |
|         |                                                 |
|         v                                                 |
| 4. Repository Staging & Signing                           |
|    - Atomic promotion to 'testing' repo pool              |
|    - Cryptographic signing with HSM / Minisign key        |
|         |                                                 |
|         v                                                 |
| 5. Automated VM Smoke Test (Headless QEMU)                |
|    - Boot ephemeral VM, verify package upgrades, halt     |
|         |                                                 |
|         v                                                 |
| 6. Production Promotion                                   |
|    - Rsync repository metadata to global mirrors          |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Topological Build Ordering

If a pull request upgrades `openssl`, dozens of downstream packages (`curl`, `python3`, `git`, `openvpn`) must be rebuilt against the new ABI.

The CI orchestrator walks the dependency graph:
1. Builds `openssl` first inside the clean base container.
2. Publishes the new `openssl.byol` package to a temporary local staging cache.
3. Injects the newly compiled library into the buildroots of `curl` and `git`.
4. Compiles the downstream packages in parallel.

## Headless QEMU Smoke Testing in CI

Never publish packages without booting an actual test machine! In modern CI environments, you can boot your custom ISO or target disk image inside a headless QEMU instance and capture exit codes:

```bash
# Automated smoke test inside GitHub Actions runner:
$ qemu-system-x86_64 \
    -enable-kvm \
    -m 2G \
    -kernel /build/vmlinuz \
    -initrd /build/initramfs.img \
    -append "console=ttyS0 byol.autotest=1 panic=5" \
    -serial stdio \
    -display none \
    | tee boot.log

# Verify that boot completed successfully:
$ grep "BYOL System Initialized Successfully" boot.log
```
If the test kernel panics or init hangs, the CI pipeline fails immediately, preventing broken releases from ever reaching user machines.
